J Clin Oncol 2005; 23: 4602–8. Malignant neoplasms of the bone. Solid cancers of- ten metastasise to the skeleton and metastatic bone disease is a common problem with cancers of the breast, prostate, and lung. Bone metastases are often responsible for cancer pain (the general management of which is discussed on p.5) and also result in immobility, bone fractures, bone- marrow failure, spinal cord compression, and hypercalcae- mia.1 The most common sites of metastasis are the spine, hip, and femur.
